grades.observed_answer: Intruders trying to move through a Closed Door destroy it and stay in their starting Room. If several attempt through the same Door together, they destroy it simultaneously and all stay. A Destroyed Door cannot later be closed again, except with the Plasma Torch. An Intruder appearing due to a Noise roll can come through a Corridor with a Closed Door; the Door does not block that appearance.
grades.reader_evidence: Fire, Malfunction, Doors, Slime and Noise markers: Closed Door movement, simultaneous movement, destroyed-door rule, and Noise appearance exception.
grades.reason: All requested material rulings resolved correctly with summary support. Equivalent phrasing accepted. Unrequested key context and cleanup not required.

grades.question: An injured Intruder moves into Technical Corridors with Noise already there. What happens to its miniature, injuries, token and Noise? Can Characters or Doors normally use those Corridors?
grades.expected_answer: Remove miniature, discard injuries, return matching token to bag; keep Noise. Characters barred except Mechanic Technical Corridors card and Technical Corridor Plans Item; Doors never placed there.
grades.observed_answer: An Intruder moving to a Technical Corridors Entrance disappears: remove its miniature, discard all Injury markers, and return its token to the bag. Noise on the Technical Corridors space remains. Characters cannot normally use Technical Corridors (only the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card and Technical Corridor Plans Item are exceptions); Doors cannot be placed there.
grades.reader_evidence: Technical Corridors section: Intruder disappearance and Character exceptions; Noise marker remains; Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.

grades.question: Describe an ordinary Shoot versus Melee Action: card/ammo costs, target location, Contamination, a miss, and the two-hit die result.
grades.expected_answer: Both cost 1 Action card against target in same Room. Shoot needs Weapon in Hand and spends 1 Ammo; normal two-hit deals 2 injuries subject to Weapon. Melee draws Contamination to Action discard before choosing target, miss causes Serious Wound, two-hit deals only 1 injury.
grades.observed_answer: Shoot costs 1 Action card, requires a Hand weapon with ammo, targets one Intruder in the Character's Room, and discards 1 Ammo. It draws no Contamination card. A blank Combat die result misses without the Melee miss penalty; a two-hit result deals 2 Injuries when Shooting, before Weapon modifications. Melee costs 1 Action card, draws a Contamination card onto the Action discard pile, and targets one Intruder in the same Room. A miss inflicts 1 Serious Wound on the Character, and the two-hit result deals only 1 Injury in Melee.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat: Shoot and Melee Attack procedures and results; Contamination cards section: received Contamination is placed on top of Action discard pile.

grades.question: After damage, how are Larva, Adult and Queen death checked, when is a Carcass placed, and what if a Queen check draws a Retreat arrow?
grades.expected_answer: Larva dies at 1 injury without Carcass. Adult draws one Attack card blood, dies if blood <= current injuries and leaves Carcass. Queen draws two, sums blood and compares same way; any Retreat arrow causes retreat via Event-card corridor number, discard Event, rather than normal numerical resolution.
grades.observed_answer: A Larva or Egg dies from 1 Injury; remove its miniature and do not place a Carcass. For Creeper or Adult, draw one Intruder Attack card and kill it if the blood value is equal to or lower than its current injuries; place a Carcass. For Queen or Breeder, draw two and add the blood values, using the same comparison; place a Carcass if killed. During an Injury Effect check, a Retreat arrow makes the Intruder flee along the Corridor number on a drawn Event card; a Queen or Breeder retreats if either of its two cards has the arrow.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat, Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat.
grades.reason: All requested material rulings resolved correctly with summary support. Equivalent phrasing accepted. Unrequested key context and cleanup not required.

grades.question: A Character Escapes a Room with two Intruders toward an empty unexplored Room. When do attacks occur, who is targeted, what happens if they die, and what follows if they survive?
grades.expected_answer: Pay Movement cost 1, choose neighboring Room. Before moving resolve separate Attack from each Intruder targeting escaper. Death leaves Corpse in starting Room; survival completes move and standard exploration/Noise.
grades.observed_answer: Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder in the Room, targeting the escaper. If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to leave. If they survive, complete the move to the neighboring Room; if it is empty, resolve a Noise roll, and if unexplored, explore it normally.

grades.question: In an ordinary Intruder Attack with several Characters, how is the target chosen and ties broken; how is a hit determined; what changes for Larva and where does its Contamination go?
grades.expected_answer: Fewest Action cards in hand; tie First Player or next in turn order. Matching attacker symbol on drawn Attack card means resolve effect; otherwise miss; ignore blood and discard card. Larva draws no Attack card: place miniature on target Character board and give Contamination on top of Action discard.
grades.observed_answer: With several Characters in the Room, target the one whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; ties go to the First Player token holder or next player in turn order. Draw an Intruder Attack card: a matching attacker symbol triggers its effect, otherwise the attack misses. A Larva instead removes its miniature from the board, places it on the target's Character board, and gives the target a Contamination card, placed on top of their Action discard pile.

grades.question: At three Serious Wounds, does dressing one prevent death from a Light Wound? What happens at a third Light Wound otherwise, what does Heal remove, and where do a dead Characters Corpse and Heavy Objects go?
grades.expected_answer: No: dressed still counts; any further Wound kills at three Serious. Third Light clears Light track and causes Serious Wound. Heal removes specified Light Wound or discards dressed Serious card. Place Corpse and drop Heavy Objects in death Room.
grades.observed_answer: Dressing a Serious Wound does not prevent death from another Wound at three Serious Wounds: dressing ignores the card's effect but it still counts toward the three-wound limit. A third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes a Serious Wound. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card, as specified by the healing effect. On death, place a Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
grades.reader_evidence: Character Wounds and death: three Serious Wounds plus any Wound kills; dressing still counts; Light Wound conversion; Heal; death and dropped objects.

grades.question: Contrast Canteen/Shower scanning with Surgery: which cards are scanned and removed, how is a Larva handled, and what costs or turn consequences follow Surgery?
grades.expected_answer: Canteen/Shower optionally scan hand Contamination, remove non-Infected; infected gives Larva and retains card, existing Larva means death/Creeper. Canteen heals 1 Light; Shower removes Slime. Surgery scans deck/hand/discard, removes infected and Larva, then 1 Light Wound, automatic pass, shuffle all cards including hand into deck; empty hand until next turn.
grades.observed_answer: Canteen and Shower scan Contamination cards in the Character's hand only, removing all non-Infected cards; an Infected result places a Larva, and if one is already present the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room. Canteen also heals 1 Light Wound; Shower also removes Slime. Surgery scans cards in the Action deck, hand, and discard pile, removes all Infected cards, removes a Larva if present, then causes 1 Light Wound and an automatic pass. Shuffle all cards, including the hand and remaining Contamination cards, into the Action deck; the hand stays empty until next turn.
grades.reader_evidence: Room Actions, Canteen/Shower/Surgery; Contamination cards section.

grades.question: How can uncarried Eggs be destroyed with Shoot/Melee, grenades, Molotov and Fire; which Melee penalties are waived, when is Noise rolled and when is the Nest destroyed?
grades.expected_answer: Each injury from Shoot/Melee destroys 1 Egg. Egg melee draws no Contamination and causes no missed-attack wound. Grenade 2 Eggs, Molotov 1; Noise after every destruction attempt including miss. Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg in Fire Damage. Nest destroyed when all Eggs taken/destroyed; mark Injury in Nest.
grades.observed_answer: In a Room with uncarried Eggs, use Shoot or Melee against them; each Injury of any type destroys one Egg. Melee against Eggs never draws Contamination, and a miss causes no Wound. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs and a Molotov destroys 1. Roll Noise after every single attempt to destroy an Egg. Fire in the Room destroys 1 uncarried Egg during each Fire Damage step. When no Eggs remain, the Nest is destroyed and marked with an Injury marker. The summary gives no further Melee penalties to waive beyond the no-Contamination and no-miss-Wound rules stated here.
grades.reader_evidence: Eggs and the Nest: destroying Eggs and Nest destruction.

grades.question: What permits or prevents entering an Escape Pod, what must you resolve first, how many Characters and Heavy Objects fit, and what are the options and consequences when you wait?
grades.expected_answer: Use corresponding Evacuation Room Action cost 2 with unlocked pod and free space, no Intruder or Malfunction; roll Noise first and fail if Intruder reaches Room. Two Character spaces; Objects use none. Enter then launch immediately or wait; launch at first-round start in later Player Phase, voluntary free exit during round, no launch automatically passes. Intruder appearing in Section returns all pod occupants to Room; another boarder may launch immediately.
grades.observed_answer: Enter using the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action (cost 2 Action cards) if the Pod is Unlocked and has a free Character space. Make a Noise roll first; entry fails if an Intruder appears or is present in the Room, and the Room Actions reference also lists a Malfunction token as preventing entry. Each Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects take no Character space. After entry, launch immediately or wait. While waiting, launch at the start of your first round in each Player Phase or exit voluntarily for free; if you do not launch in your round, you automatically pass. If an Intruder appears in the Evacuation Room while waiting, all pod occupants return to that Room; another Character entering your Pod may launch it immediately.
grades.reader_evidence: Escape Pods section and Room Actions, Evacuation Section A/B.

grades.question: Give the endgame checks in order. What happens with two Damaged Engines, a non-Earth destination (including Quarantine/Mars), and an infected survivor or one carrying a Larva? Do pod passengers need Contamination checks?
grades.expected_answer: Engines then Coordinates then Contamination then Objectives. If ship survives to checks: two/three Damaged explodes kills all aboard incl Intruders; non-Earth kills sleepers but ship/Intruders survive, Quarantine sleeper survives Mars. All survivors including launched pod passengers scan all Contamination; any infected triggers shuffle all Action/Contamination draw 4, any Contamination kills else survives. Larva skips scanning and directly does shuffle/draw. Survivors then reveal/check chosen Objective.
grades.observed_answer: Victory checks are Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, then Objectives. If two or three Engines are Damaged, the ship explodes; hibernating Characters die. If the destination is not Earth, hibernating Characters die, except a Character with the Quarantine Objective survives hibernation if the destination is Mars. An infected survivor scans all Contamination cards in deck, discard pile, and hand; if at least one is Infected, shuffle all cards and draw four, dying if any Contamination card appears among them. A survivor carrying a Larva skips the scan step and resolves the draw-four test directly. Evacuated pod survivors are included in the Contamination check, so they do need that check.
grades.reader_evidence: Victory Check: Engines, Coordinates, Contamination; applies to each surviving Character 'hibernating or evacuated.'
grades.reason: Engine failure effects omit that Intruders/everything else aboard dies; infection procedure otherwise resolved.
